rationale: Evidence: iteration 7 (kd 0.30, kp 4.0, ki 0.3, sensor_size 0.012, sensors at y 0.06) scored 93.70, the best raced design, up from 84.33. Its oval steering_oscillation is 0.246, under the 0.25 threshold, so the kd step is kept as the new base, as the Evaluator's rule requires. max_error is still 0.061 to 0.065 m on every track, and every run still goes off track with one line-loss event. Gain changes (kp, ki, kd), the sensor footprint (0.016) and sensor y (0.04 to 0.06) have all been tried without moving that floor. Per the Evaluator's requested next step, this iteration tests the sensor x spread on the iteration 7 base, changing only that variable. Change: sensor x positions narrow from -0.04..0.04 to -0.03..0.03 (spacing 0.015 m), at y 0.06 and sensor_size 0.012. Weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], kp 4.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.30, base_speed 1.3 and last_direction are unchanged. Hypothesis: a narrower array keeps the outer sensors on the tape during tight bends and reduces the off-track excursion, so max_error should fall below about 0.060 m and line_loss_events should drop. The risk is that a narrower array gives less signal on wide bends and lowers the score. Expected result: score at or above 93.70 is not assured; this is a test. If the score falls below 93.70, or oval steering_oscillation exceeds 0.25, return to x -0.04..0.04 (iteration 7 geometry). If max_error is unchanged, the next lever is a wider spread (for example x -0.06..0.06, within the contract limit of 0.08). Do not raise base_speed until progress nears 0.995 with no line loss. Completion within 3 s is not expected at base_speed 1.3.
